A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain of vertebrates from mammals to fishes contain a proline endoprotease and a pyrogultamyl aminopeptidase which degrade TRH in vitro to TRH-OH.
the peptidases of the brain of lower and higher vertebrates have a similar capacity to degrade TRH to TRH-OH and cyclo(His- Pro).

The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain TRH in lower vertebrates is metabolized by peptidases that produce the same two metabolites that are found in mammalian species.
TRH is inactivated in all the species studied by peptidases in both the soluble and particulate fractions.
TRH and its metabolites are present in the brain of all vertebrate species and are degraded by similar peptidase mechanisms.
